3. Recommended Alignment Alternate
The alignment studies for Lincoln Highway were made after full and careful consideration of the existing Comprehensive Plans of the Villages of Park Forest, Matteson and Olympia Fields as well as that of the City of Chicago Heights.
The two alternates for the proposed improvement should not change the basic characteristics of the presently developed area through which it passes. Present development along Lincoln Highway includes residential areas, retail stores, service industries, automobile-oriented businesses and vacant land. The four communities served by this section of Lincoln Highway each have land-use maps prepared by planning consultants, although the plans have not been officially accepted by the communities. These plans, however, are in general use and with few exceptions the land-use patterns proposed by the planners are developing on the ground. A composite land-use plan is shown as Exhibit "7", page I-15.
Much of the property along Lincoln Highway is or will be part of a strip development, at least one block deep, primarily involved in automobileoriented or other highway businesses, interlaced with retail stores. Those residential areas in Chicago Heights that front on Lincoln Highway can be expected to become business properties within the lifetime of this improvement. The residential property in Park Forest, however, should retain its present classification as the property faces away from the highway. The undeveloped land in Olympia Fields, which lies between the Illinois Central Railroad and Western Avenue, also is developing with residential lots facing away from the highway and should keep this portion of Lincoln Highway residential in nature.
That portion of Olympia Fields west of the Illinois Central Railroad already is developing as a highway-oriented business district. It probably will continue to develop that way on the north side of Lincoln Highway from Olympian Way west to the western side of Evergreen Street where, again, residential property faces away from the highway.
